comment: The rules of D3.5 and D6.9 that close two routes to a forged pointer. The `.ptr` of a span or a
string stands in two positions only, each as it stands: an argument of an `extern fn` that can
give fort code no pointer that does not say `own`, at any level and in any struct field, and an
operand of `==` or `!=`. No cast and no `str.from_cstr` takes a `.ptr` (D3.5). Only
`str.from_cstr` and `rt.args_init` take `p[lo..hi]` of a raw pointer, and no source names
`rt.args_init` (D6.9). The rows cover src/fort/check.ft: pseudo_field, has_ptr_argument,
give_enter, give_step, give_run, c_gives_pointer, the variable tail of check_call,
is_pseudo_ptr, the operands of `==` and `!=` in check_expr, raw_span_allowed, is_args_init,
check_span_expr and value_of_sym. The first stage runs the language tests of the two rules,
whose goldens pin each message and its position. The second runs check_raw_span_test.ft, which
holds the two functions in a sandbox std, and check_ptr_walk_limit_test.ft, the one witness of
the work limit of the walk. The table runs in the VM with the debug preset: pass a --runner
that runs tools/vm run in one slot, as notes/environment.md says. The md5 guard reads the
product compiler. The first round of a run in the VM can read stale (notes/testing.md 1), so
run the first row again before you trust it.
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort

stages.name: the language tests of the two rules
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 4 fail/spans/007 fail/stdlib/007 fail/stdlib/008 fail/pointers/009 fail/pointers/010 fail/ffi/013 fail/ffi/014 fail/ffi/015 fail/ffi/016 run/pointers/004 run/pointers/014 run/stdlib/013 run/stdlib/068 run/stdlib/125 run/stdlib/126

stages.name: the checker suites of the two functions and of the work limit
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 300 -j 2 check_raw_span_test check_ptr_walk_limit_test
